name: Huelva
title: Huelva Tanker & Bulk Carrier UTM | Ship Thickness Gauging
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Huelva for crude, product and chemical tankers, gas carriers and bulk carriers: cargo and ballast tanks, holds and deck piping.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement at the Port of Huelva: Tankers, Gas and Bulk
intro: Huelva is Andalusia's Atlantic energy and chemicals port, at the junction of the Odiel and Tinto rivers. Crude and product tankers serve a refinery, gas carriers serve a regasification terminal, and bulk carriers bring ore concentrates and raw materials for a metals and chemicals complex. Technicians travel from India to the ship for ultrasonic gauging, planned within terminal permit rules and the tidal channel's working pattern.

highlights.p: Crude, product and chemical tankers call at dedicated terminals. We gauge decks, ballast tanks, pump rooms and, once gas-free, cargo tanks, working to each terminal's permit and hot-work rules.

highlights.h: Gas carriers at the regasification terminal
highlights.p: Hull plating, ballast tanks and deck structure on gas carriers can be measured during the call, within the terminal's boarding rules. Cargo containment remains outside what ultrasonic gauging covers.

highlights.h: Last stop before the Atlantic or the Strait
highlights.p: Huelva sits near the Portuguese border, close to routes between the Atlantic and the Strait of Gibraltar. Gauging here is a practical way to prepare a ship for a docking at Cádiz or a yard further along.

port.h: Huelva: refinery, chemicals and metals on a tidal estuary
p: The port of Huelva follows the estuary formed where the Odiel and Tinto rivers meet before the Atlantic, with an outer breakwater, a dredged approach channel and quays along the Odiel and at the chemical zone near Palos de la Frontera. Tides matter here: deeper-draught ships plan arrival and sailing around high water, and the channel's width and depth govern how large a ship can come. The Autoridad Portuaria de Huelva runs the harbour, and pilotage is compulsory for most ships.

Energy and industry dominate. A large refinery at La Rábida takes crude and ships products, while a chemical and fertiliser complex handles liquid and dry bulk raw materials. A copper smelter imports concentrates by sea, and a regasification terminal gives the port a place on the LNG map. Bulk carriers, tankers and gas carriers are therefore the main callers. Cruise and passenger traffic are minor, and the port also supports a fishing fleet, tugs and pilot boats, together with dredgers working to keep the channel open.

Inspection needs reflect that cargo. Tankers carrying crude and chemicals are surveyed on the enhanced programme, and their owners want thickness data on cargo and ballast tank boundaries, deck plating and pipework. Bulk carriers carrying concentrates and fertiliser raw materials suffer chemical as well as mechanical wear in their holds, because some cargoes are corrosive when damp. Gauging at Huelva helps owners decide which tanks or holds need attention before the next survey, and it gives a baseline for ships that run between the Atlantic coast and Mediterranean ports.

facilities.h: Gauging locations around the Odiel and Tinto estuary
p: Most work takes place alongside at the terminals. Tankers at the refinery and chemical berths are gauged under the terminal's permit-to-work arrangements, starting with deck, pump room and ballast tanks and extending to cargo tanks once they are gas-free and certified safe for entry. Bulk carriers at the dry-bulk quays are gauged hold by hold during and after discharge, with extra attention to tank tops and lower frames where corrosive cargo has lain. Gas carriers at the regasification terminal follow the terminal's own boarding rules, and the scope is restricted to hull structure, ballast tanks, deck and piping outside the containment.

Ship repair in Huelva is on a small scale, suited to tugs, fishing vessels and workboats, so larger vessels normally dock at bigger yards, with Cádiz bay the natural choice nearby, or at Seville. Readings taken in Huelva form the steel list for that docking, and technicians can attend the yard for post-blast gauging. The anchorage outside the entrance is usable for pre-arrival gauging by launch in calm weather, though the Atlantic swell limits it, and ships waiting for tide or berth sometimes provide a window.
list: Refinery and oil terminal berths: deck, pump room, ballast and cargo tank gauging on crude and product tankers under terminal permits
Chemical and fertiliser quays: tank and hold readings on chemical tankers and bulk carriers handling industrial raw materials
Metal concentrate and dry-bulk berths: hold frame and tank top gauging on bulk carriers during and after discharge
Regasification terminal berth: hull, ballast and deck readings on gas carriers during their call
Repair quays and small yards: tugs, fishing vessels and workboats on the estuary
Anchorage off the entrance: occasional pre-arrival gauging by launch in settled weather

context.h: Regulation and trade drivers on the Andalusian Atlantic coast
p: Port state control for the Paris MoU is carried out in Huelva by inspectors from the Capitanía Marítima under the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante. Tankers and gas carriers are an inspection priority because of the consequences of failure, and chemical and oil tanker structure is a recurring focus of class and charterer vetting. Charterers who vet tankers often ask for recent thickness data on tanks and decks, and older ships carry that burden more heavily, which is why gauging ahead of a vetting inspection is common.

Beyond inspection, EU rules push owners to look at structure. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime raise the stakes for fuel-hungry ships, and owners choosing retrofits such as energy-saving devices or wash-water systems need to know that nearby steel is sound. The Ship Recycling Regulation's Inventory of Hazardous Materials applies to ships calling at EU ports, which makes sales and end-of-life planning for older tankers and bulkers a regular subject. A gauging report is the structural counterpart to those planning documents.

jobs.p: Requests come from tanker and bulk owners preparing for survey or charterer inspection, and from buyers and sellers of older tonnage. Each job is scoped with the superintendent against the ship's survey status and the terminal's rules, and the team travels from India with portable gauges and magnetic particle equipment. Cargo tank entry is arranged by the ship under its own gas-freeing procedures. Common examples include:
list: Deck, ballast tank and cargo tank boundary gauging on a product tanker discharging at the refinery berths, prepared for a renewal survey.
Cargo tank and pipework readings on a chemical tanker for a charterer's vetting, with attention to tank tops and bulkhead stiffeners.
Hold frame and tank top gauging on a bulk carrier unloading concentrates, measured against diminution limits in each hold.
Hull, ballast tank and deck gauging on a gas carrier lying at the regasification terminal, within the terminal's boarding rules.
Pre-docking gauging of a tanker's ballast tanks and double bottom, producing a steel estimate for a yard in Cádiz bay.

logistics: Technicians fly from India through a European hub to Seville, the nearest major airport, or to Faro across the Portuguese border, and complete the journey to Huelva by road. Terminal access is arranged by the ship's agent, who also organises launches for anchorage work. Indian nationals need a Schengen visa for Spain, so travel is planned once it is issued, and since tankers and gas carriers often have fixed discharge windows, we confirm the berth and dates with the superintendent before booking.

faqs.q: Can cargo tanks on a tanker be gauged at Huelva?
faqs.a: Yes, once the ship has gas-freed the tanks and issued an entry permit, and the terminal agrees to the work alongside. We measure bulkheads, tank tops, bottom and deck plating and stiffeners, and report by plate and frame. Deck, pump room and ballast tank readings can proceed earlier, since they do not depend on cargo tank gas-freeing.

faqs.q: Does corrosive bulk cargo change what is gauged in the holds?
faqs.a: It focuses attention on tank tops, lower frames and hopper boundaries where damp, aggressive cargo has lain. Chemical wear can be uneven, so readings are taken on a grid and compared with earlier survey figures. We also look at hatch cover skirts and coaming bases, where residue and moisture collect.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Huelva for large ships?
faqs.a: The port's repair capacity is limited to smaller vessels. Larger ships normally dock at yards in the Bay of Cádiz or elsewhere in Andalusia. Gauging in Huelva before the docking gives the yard a steel list in advance, and technicians can attend the dock for post-blast readings if the owner wants confirmation.

faqs.q: How does the tidal channel affect gauging schedules?
faqs.a: Deeper ships enter and leave on the tide, so berthing and sailing times are fixed by high water and the pilot's plan. We schedule around the confirmed berth time and keep travel flexible, because a delayed arrival is common. Once alongside, the work proceeds against the discharge or loading programme in the usual way.

faqs.q: Can gauging be combined with a charterer's tanker vetting?
faqs.a: It can be a sensible preparation. Recent thickness readings on tanks, deck and piping give the master and superintendent facts to show the vetting inspector, and highlight weak areas to deal with beforehand. We deliver readings in a plain, plate-by-plate format that the owner can pass on to the charterer.
